query: FeCoNi is an fcc alloy with high saturation magnetization and a low coercive field. Earlier studies examined the high-entropy alloys FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt, but both exhibited soft ferromagnetism. A qualifying high-entropy alloy must have an almost equiatomic multicomponent composition and configurational entropy of at least 1.0R. Subject to these constraints, what single intervention could produce a FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy with greater coercivity than the prior derivatives? Present one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the outcome relative to an appropriate FeCoNi-based baseline, defines the conditions over which it should apply, cites supporting observations from earlier work, and proposes a discriminating experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Replacing the Pd or Pt component with Ir in an equiatomic FeCoNi-based high‐entropy alloy will increase the coercivity relative to the soft ferromagnetic FeCoNiPd/Pt analogues.
generation.material_initial_state: An equiatomic FeCoNiPd (or FeCoNiPt) high‐entropy alloy with a disordered fcc structure exhibiting high saturation magnetization and low coercivity.
generation.intervention: Substitute the heavy element (Pd/Pt) with Ir to form an equiatomic FeCoNiIr alloy while maintaining the multicomponent, high configuration entropy state.
generation.conditions: The alloy will be synthesized by induction melting followed by homogenization annealing under inert atmosphere to ensure a single phase fcc solid solution. Magnetic properties will be measured at room temperature using a vibrating sample magnetometer under comparable loading (magnetic field sweep) conditions.
generation.structural_mediator: The homogeneous fcc solid solution with Ir incorporated into the lattice provides a modified local electronic environment.
generation.mechanism: Ir has a stronger spin–orbit coupling than Pd or Pt, which is expected to enhance the magnetocrystalline anisotropy. This increased anisotropy provides higher domain-wall pinning, thereby increasing the coercivity. The intervention does not disrupt the high-entropy and equiatomic nature but rather adjusts the magnetic energy landscape at the atomic scale.
generation.predicted_outcome: An observable increase in coercivity (i.e., a higher coercive field) compared to the FeCoNiPd/Pt baseline, while largely retaining the high saturation magnetization characteristic of the FeCoNi-based alloys.
generation.baseline: FeCoNiPd or FeCoNiPt high-entropy alloys that show soft ferromagnetic behavior with low coercivity.
generation.boundary: This outcome is expected if a single-phase, chemically homogeneous fcc solid solution is maintained. If Ir substitution were to cause secondary phase precipitation, ordering phenomena, or significant changes in microstructure (e.g., grain refinement unrelated to anisotropy), the magnetic behavior might deviate from the prediction.
generation.uncertainty: The magnitude of coercivity enhancement is uncertain; the actual increase depends on how strongly the Ir-induced spin–orbit coupling translates to enhanced anisotropy in the specific fcc environment. Additionally, there is some uncertainty regarding any potential impacts on saturation magnetization.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize two alloys: one equiatomic FeCoNiIr and one control alloy (e.g., FeCoNiPd) using identical induction melting and inert-atmosphere homogenization annealing protocols. Characterize both by XRD to confirm a single-phase fcc structure and then measure their magnetic hysteresis loops with a vibrating sample magnetometer at room temperature.
measurements: XRD to confirm phase and chemical homogeneity
Magnetic hysteresis loop to record coercivity (Hc)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the FeCoNiIr alloy does not exhibit a significant increase (e.g., at least 50% higher coercive field) compared to the control FeCoNiPd alloy under identical conditions—or if an unforeseen secondary phase appears that could account for the change—then the hypothesis is falsified.
